main_text.p: crassa : utá ἥω pono, δῶ do, τίθημι, δί-δωμι. Interdum nihil reduplicatur: ut νίκάω, νίκημι, vinco: φιλέω, φίλημι, amo: γνόω, γνῶμι, nosco. In polysyllabis nihil unquam reduplicatur: ut ἐλά-Ἡρωμι libero, ab ἐλάΘρεύω. Poëtæ nihil reduplicant, & reduplicationem, ut incrementum, pro metri sui commodo retinent aut tollunt. Interdum geminatur reduplicatio : ἀλάω erro, ἀλάλημι: ἀχέω doleo, ἀκάχημι. Poëtæ deducunt etiam á barytonis : ἔχω habeo ἔχημι, φέρω fero φέρημι : vel potius tanquam ab ἐχῶ, φερῶ. Bœoti præfigunt ε pro ι: ut θνάω moriar, τέθνημι: τλάω tolero, τέτλημι. Bœoti item vertunt ν in ζ, πεφίλημι, πεφίλζμι. Altera igitur anomalia conjugationis est in μι, differtque etiam aorifto secundo. Sunt autem pauca verba in μι.

page.notes: Greek words are only approximately legible in the scan, especially accents and breathings; several Greek forms are marked as uncertain in the text above where I could not confirm them letter by letter. The paragraph ending "Præsens 1," is a short centred line and may be a section label. Faint marks in the margins are not text.
